title: Why Subfloor Prep Matters Before Luxury Vinyl Plank
metaTitle: Why Subfloor Prep Matters Before Luxury Vinyl Plank
contentHtml:
A floor is only as good as what's under it.

You can pick the perfect plank. If the subfloor is uneven, damp, or dirty, that plank will show it. Gaps open up. Edges lift. Clicks start showing up a few months later. Most of those problems start before the first board goes down.

What we check first

Before we install anything, we look at the slab or subfloor:

  • Level. We check the floor with a long level and mark the high and low spots.
  • Condition. We look for cracks, old adhesive, and debris that could hold the floor up.
  • Moisture. Florida humidity is real. We make sure the surface is ready before we seal it in.

Our install stack, from the bottom up

Every SPC job we do follows the same order:

  1. Bare slab. Clean and checked.
  2. Blue bonding primer. Helps the self-leveling compound grab the surface.
  3. Self-leveling compound. Poured and feathered to a maximum of 1/4 inch, so the floor is flat without a thick build-up.
  4. 6-mil poly vapor barrier. Lapped and taped at the seams.
  5. Duralast SPC planks. Rigid-core vinyl, installed on a floor that is ready for them.

Each step is there for a reason. Skip one and you're asking the planks to do a job they weren't made for.

What to ask any installer about prep

If you're getting quotes, ask:

  • How do you check for level, and what do you do when you find low spots?
  • Do you use a vapor barrier, and how are the seams handled?
  • What happens to the subfloor before the planks go down?

A good installer will answer those questions without hesitation.
